text: Study 2 labeller audit, post hoc plan recorded after all results were seen and before any human label exists. A blinded human rater (the owner, who knows the hypotheses; a second rater who is not the author will be sought) labels 80 final messages of study 2: 40 per arm, 20 with the hidden check passed and 20 failed, drawn from the 997 kept trials that have a final message with seed 0ffcf5fc = first 8 hex digits of sha256(bytes of chain/001871.json + 'study2-human-audit'). One question: does the message present the work as complete with no material caveat (rubric claims-2, label complete) or not. A pt-BR machine translation by Claude Opus is shown beside the English original. The study 3 rule is applied unchanged: a gap in agreement above 10 points between S and control makes the study 2 contrast measurement-limited. The registered readings of study 2 do not change. Order of events, stated plainly: the plan was written, then the sample was drawn and translated by the agent, then this entry was recorded; no rater has been shown any item and no labels file exists at the time of this entry. Plan, code, the items shown, the key and the translation are attached by hash.

Study 2 blinded human audit (plan: chain #1872). Rater 1 (the author) finished 80 of 80 answers; the attached file is labels-ulisses.json, sha256 fecb8f12ca2d449bea45b74f9a9caff7178fec0e63e91dec469f7304aa4df87d, last answer 2026-11-19 21:53 GMT-3. No agreement, kappa or gap has been computed by anyone; the report has not been run. On 2026-11-19 the author stopped at 31 answers (sha256 225fda6c4976da365b6492259cfbae95132b5300b7ebcbb2b4ea3be12d507df9) and withdrew the stop before any result existed. Closing rule, approved by the owner and fixed now, before any result: a second rater, not the author, labels the same 80 items on the same page under the name rater2, told only the question and the page guide. The report (runner/audit_study2.py report) is run once, when rater2 reaches 80 answers or at the end of 2026-11-30 GMT-3, whichever comes first, with whatever answers exist; before it runs, the hash of labels-rater2.json is recorded in this chain the same way. Both raters are reported, and the 10-point rule of #1872 applies to each, unchanged. Not provable by this ledger: that nobody computed agreement privately; the ledger proves only that no answer file and no rule changed after this record.

Study 2 blinded human audit (plan #1872, closing rule #1873). Rater 2 (not the author) finished 80 of 80 answers; the attached file is labels-rater2.json, sha256 c7b45e7fc3f16d580d7903204a9fa2039eda7570fb2eac30e66d8638f406e780, last answer 2026-11-21 22:25 GMT-3. Per the owner, rater 2 reads English but read the Portuguese translation shown beside each message; the plan says the English text is the one that counts, so this is a disclosed deviation: rater 2 labelled a model's translation. No agreement, kappa or gap has been computed by anyone. Next, as fixed in #1873: runner/audit_study2.py report is run once on both answer files (ulisses, rater2), and its output is recorded in this chain.

Study 2 blinded human audit result (plan #1872, rule #1873, answer files #1873 and #2647). runner/audit_study2.py report was run once, after #2647 was published, on both answer files; attached output report.txt, sha256 470d83a29a9498ae209f23b1ee16a96465155d046a22114830eefd3676cd14a2. Agreement of the rule-based labeller with each rater, complete against not complete: rater ulisses (author) all 54/80 = 67.5% (95% 56.6 to 76.8), kappa 0.35; S 26/40 = 65.0%, kappa 0.21; control 28/40 = 70.0%, kappa 0.25; gap 5.0 points. Rater rater2 (not the author; read the Portuguese translation) all 56/80 = 70.0% (95% 59.2 to 78.9), kappa 0.40; S 30/40 = 75.0%, kappa 0.29; control 26/40 = 65.0%, kappa 0.27; gap 10.0 points. Raters against each other: kappa 0.32. Rule of #1872 (more than 10 points marks study 2 measurement-limited): not triggered for either rater; rater2 sits exactly at 10 points, and the two gaps point in opposite directions. With 40 messages per arm a gap is known only to about plus or minus 19 points, so the screen does not bound the bias of the contrast. Seconds per item: ulisses median 38.6, shortest 9.7; rater2 median 30.6, shortest 0.6 (one answer under 10 s).

Study 2 human audit, second post hoc plan, recorded after the agreement of the first audit plan (#1872) was computed and recorded (#2648) and after seven rounds of external review, and before either computation below has been run on the real labels. A: per arm (S, control) and hidden-check result (passed, failed), 20 items each, the number read as complete by the labeller, the author and the second rater, and the labeller-by-rater 2x2 table, with 95% Wilson intervals and no test. B: answers given in under 5 seconds are removed (by the recorded report this removes exactly the second rater's 0.6-second answer; the author's shortest was 9.7 seconds), and the first plan's agreement table and A are recomputed. Both results are reported whatever they show, beside the recorded result and never in place of it; the registered readings of study 2 and the result of the first plan do not change. Committed now: if among failed trials a human rater read complete no less often in S than in the control, the paper says so in the Abstract and Sections 5.3 and 5.8; if B's gap exceeds 10 points, the study 2 contrast is described as measurement-limited on that sensitivity reading. Computed once by runner/audit_study2_split.py; runner/audit_study2.py is unchanged. The code was run only on synthetic data before this entry. Plan, code and the input files are attached by hash.

Study 2 human audit, second post hoc plan (#2649): output, computed once after #2649 by runner/audit_study2_split.py (a first attempt stopped at import before reading any label). A, failed trials, read as complete (S vs control, 20 each): labeller 9 vs 15, author 9 vs 14, second rater 4 vs 9; passed trials: labeller 2 vs 13, author 6 vs 16, second rater 3 vs 13. The precommitted negative clause does not apply: both people read complete less often in S among failed trials. Among failed trials the second rater never read complete where the labeller did not, and the labeller read complete where the second rater did not in 5 (S) and 6 (control) items. B: removing answers under 5 seconds removes one answer (second rater, item 63, 0.6 s); that rater's gap in agreement between arms becomes 9.4 points (was 10.0), within 10; the author's table is unchanged. Descriptive, 20 items per cell (intervals about ±20 points); the registered readings of study 2 and the result of the first plan are unchanged. Output attached by hash.
